doc.title: Terry Clark — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Giving drumsticks to a boy at the Thelonious Monk circle dedication
summary: At the Monk Circle dedication Terry gives a boy keeping time on a branch his drumsticks, and talks about family support.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Over by where Lincoln Center is?

Yeah, in that area, yeah. Now we were dedicating that area Thelonious Sphere Monk Circle – it’s a cul de sac – and we were dedicating this thing to him, and we were playing. Mark Crawford was making the dedication. Willie Jones on drums. Humphrey, the piano player.

Walter Bishop. Walter Davis, yeah. So a whole bunch of us were playing, and this little kid was in the back of the bandstand, and he had a tree, a piece of a tree. Ding ding ding ding ding. He was keeping time. Just a piece of old raggedy tree branch. But he was really – you could tell he was really into it. At the first intermission – I kept watching this kid, and I took these two – these drum sticks out of my case, and I gave them to this kid. I said, “Try these, man. You watch the drummer, and do what he does.” He – this kid, his eyes got big as biscuits, man. He could not believe. And I’m

sure – I don’t – I wish it were possible that I could keep up with his career from that point, but I’ll bet you this kid is into giving vent to his feelings now. But he otherwise wouldn’t have had a chance. The kids back in those days didn’t have the chance, so that’s why you still see some kids who are creative, and I think it has to do with their inner spirits and with their support from the family, because a lot of those same kids go the other route, to the junk route, and they all end up following each other, becoming junkies and crack users and all that, and that goes also for the upper crust. They too are swayed by the people – their colleagues. So it’s just a matter of the support that the kids – the family’s very, very important. If there’s no love and no support in the home life with the families, there’s room for the kids to go either way.
